changes: Azure accelerated to 48% ($33.2bn, +$3.7bn QoQ) and is guided to 49-50% in 2Q, above the 46-47% buy-side bar, while management still says demand exceeds supply.

Capex including finance leases was $45.2bn, about 11% below StreetAccount's $50.7bn and Microsoft's own 'over $50bn', because third-party (neocloud) capacity deliveries slipped. CY26 capex view cut to about $170bn from about $175bn.

Microsoft is now a borrower: hours after Hood said debt markets were available but not yet tapped, it launched a 10-tranche, at-least-$25bn bond sale (first US high-grade deal since 2017), talked at T+50-55bp (2-year) to T+130-135bp (40-year).

Backlog stalled: commercial RPO $677bn vs $678bn at 30 June; growth slowed to 73% from 84%; commercial bookings fell 12% (single source). OpenAI revenue was $10.0bn in the quarter (10.8% of revenue vs 7.3% in FY26).

Leases not yet commenced rose $35.5bn in one quarter to $364.6bn (now FY27-FY34), and operating-lease additions jumped to $6.5bn from $1.4bn a year earlier, confirming the shift of future data center leases off reported capex.

consensus_thesis: Investors own Microsoft as the capacity-constrained AI cloud whose 45%-plus Azure growth and $678bn commercial RPO justify capex above $50bn a quarter, funded from its own cash flow by a AAA balance sheet.
headline: The consensus view should hold and tilt up on Azure, but drop the 'self-funded' assumption: Microsoft is still compounding, yet its AI build is now financed with bonds and $364.6bn of uncommenced leases as well as cash, so credit quality stays very high but no longer improves.
kona: Microsoft just showed who carries delivery risk: when third-party capacity slipped, it simply spent about $5bn less and kept growing Azure, while CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN fell 5-6% after hours. Kona should expect any hyperscaler-grade tenancy to pay only from delivery and to price its own schedule risk, so on-time power at Vaca Muerta is the product, and Kona should prefer selling power or hosting a GPU owner over owning GPUs against a delivery-gated contract. Microsoft also prefers leasing ($35.5bn of new uncommenced leases this quarter) and can borrow at AAA spreads, so a powered, lease-ready shell is easier to sell to it than GPU-as-a-service.
monitor: 2Q FY27 capex 'over $50bn' and whether delayed third-party capacity actually lands in 2H; any change to the CY26 $170bn view.
Final size and pricing of the bond deal (settles 4 November) and whether Microsoft becomes a regular issuer like Alphabet (twice a year).
Commercial RPO and bookings: does RPO resume growth from $677bn, and does OpenAI's share of revenue (10.8%) keep rising?

sections.body: More: Engineering efficiency across GPUs, CPUs, memory and storage as a source of Azure capacity; Foundry and token pricing; Maia and Cobalt chips; 24 new data centers; 'fungible fleet'; financing flexibility. Less or dropped: Copilot seat numbers (no update, after 30mn paid seats in July); RPO excluding OpenAI (25% in July, not repeated in sources read); GW or MW added (never given). KPIs more important: Capex including finance leases versus plan (now a delivery metric for neoclouds); leases not yet commenced; OpenAI revenue and receivable; debt outstanding. Less: Book net cash as a signal of self-funding (it fell to $29.0bn and bonds will add gross debt). Risks up: Funding: first new-money bonds since 2017. Counterparty: OpenAI receivable $7.2bn (from $6.0bn). Third-party delivery: neocloud slips cut capex by about $5bn. Risks down: Azure deceleration and margin compression: both receded this quarter.

head: Question
Why it matters / asked?
rows: You said debt markets were available but 'not yet tapped' on 28 October and launched a $25bn+ deal on 29 October. Is this a one-off or the start of semi-annual issuance like Alphabet's? What leverage ceiling keeps you AAA?
Credit. Sets the end of self-funded AI capex. Asked (Liani); answered partially before the deal.

Leases not yet commenced rose $35.5bn to $364.6bn in one quarter. How much is conditional on power or construction milestones, and how much is operating rather than finance? Will you report capex plus new lease commitments each quarter?
Credit. Debt-like obligations now 5.1x finance lease liabilities. Not asked.

Third-party deliveries slipped enough to cut 1Q capex by about $5bn versus your plan. Which providers, how many MW, and do your contracts give you termination or step-in rights if 2H deliveries also slip?
Credit for neocloud lenders. Not asked.
Commercial RPO was $677bn, flat on June, and bookings fell 12%. What is RPO growth excluding OpenAI, and what share of RPO is OpenAI at 30 September?
Equity. Backlog quality. Not asked; not disclosed.
OpenAI revenue was $10.0bn (10.8% of revenue) and its receivable rose to $7.2bn. How much of OpenAI's commitment is prepaid or collateralized?
Equity and credit. Asked indirectly (Borges); deflected.

About three-quarters of capex went to short-lived assets and you used $6.7bn more cash to secure components. Will you change server useful lives, and what does a one-year change do to FY27 operating income?
Equity. GPU residual value. Not asked.
